label: Sedan
description: Mid-size four-door passenger car. The default other-vehicle: use it for lead, following and oncoming traffic when nothing special is required.

label: Hatchback
description: Compact five-door hatchback. Short, agile city car — good for tight parking rows and gap-acceptance scenarios.

label: SUV
description: Mid-size sport-utility vehicle. Tall enough to hide a child or a cyclist from a following driver; the common suburban parked vehicle.

label: Pickup truck
description: Full-size crew-cab pickup with an open bed. Long and tall; a parked one at a kerb blocks the sightline into a driveway.

label: Cargo van
description: High-roof delivery van. A double-parked one is the canonical occluder for a pedestrian stepping out mid-block.

label: Box truck
description: Two-axle straight truck with a 24 ft cargo body. Completely blocks the sightline across an adjacent lane.

label: Semi tractor-trailer
description: Conventional tractor with a 53 ft box trailer. The strongest mobile occluder in the catalog and the reference articulated vehicle for turning and blind-spot cases.

label: Transit bus
description: Forty-foot city bus with kerb-side doors. Stopped at a bus stop it hides boarding and alighting pedestrians from through traffic.

label: Motorcycle
description: Standard motorcycle, no rider. Narrow silhouette used for lane-filtering, late-detection and misclassification cases.

label: Cyclist
description: Bicycle with a seated rider. The reference vulnerable road user for bike-lane, dooring and right-hook conflicts.

label: Ambulance
description: Box-body emergency ambulance with a roof light bar. Use lights.emergency and audio.horn timeline state keys for emergency-response conflicts.

label: Tram / streetcar
description: Single articulated urban tram for rail-crossing, mixed-traffic and platform conflicts. Its long fixed-path body is a strong moving occluder.

label: Mobility scooter
description: Low-speed powered mobility scooter with a seated rider. Treat as a vulnerable road user for crossing and sidewalk-edge interactions.

label: Adult standing
description: Adult pedestrian at rest, 1.75 m. Use at kerbs, refuge islands and bus stops where the person is waiting rather than crossing.

label: Adult walking
description: Adult pedestrian in a mid-stride pose, 1.75 m. Use for crossings and for anyone the ego must yield to.

label: Child standing
description: Child pedestrian at rest, 1.20 m — short enough to be hidden by a parked sedan. Top-heavy proportions on purpose.

label: Child walking
description: Child pedestrian mid-stride, 1.20 m. The darting-child case: pair with a parked-vehicle occluder.

label: Traffic marshal / police director
description: High-visibility traffic marshal with a raised directing arm. Use pose.gesture timeline states to halt or wave traffic through.

label: Traffic cone
description: Standard 700 mm orange channelizing cone with two reflective bands. The unit of any taper or lane closure.

label: Channelizer drum
description: Plastic 1070 mm drum with four reflective bands. Delineates long-duration work areas; more conspicuous than a cone.

label: Type III barricade
description: Full 8 ft type-III barricade with three striped rails and a warning light. Used to close a road or a ramp outright.

label: Pedestrian barrier
description: Lightweight interlocking crowd-control barrier used to separate pedestrians from a temporary traffic lane or event egress route.

label: Jersey barrier
description: Single precast concrete barrier segment, 10 ft. Hard separation between live traffic and a work area.

label: Jersey barrier run
description: Continuous line of jersey barriers of a given length, running along +X. Use to wall off a work zone or a contraflow.

label: Road work sign
description: Orange 48 in diamond warning sign on a portable stand (ROAD WORK AHEAD style), facing +X. Place upstream of every closure.

label: Flagger
description: Worker in a hi-vis vest and hard hat holding a STOP/SLOW paddle out to the side. A vulnerable road user standing in the roadway.

label: Arrow board trailer
description: Trailer-mounted flashing arrow board directing traffic left or right. Sits at the start of a lane-closure taper.

label: Excavator
description: Tracked excavator with the boom stowed forward. A large static machine inside a work area; blocks sightlines completely.

label: Portable toilet
description: Site toilet cabin, 2.3 m tall on a 1.16 m footprint. Small, very tall occluder often parked right at a kerb line.

label: Spoil pile
description: Heap of excavated soil and broken pavement. Low, irregular obstacle that narrows the drivable surface.

label: Temporary stop sign
description: Portable octagonal stop sign on a weighted work-zone stand for temporary right-of-way control and alternating one-lane traffic.

label: Portable traffic signal
description: Trailer-mounted temporary red/amber/green signal head used to control alternating traffic through a work zone.

label: Long construction pipe
description: Eight-metre utility pipe laid beside or partly across a work zone. A rigid collidable obstacle and low sight-line blocker.

label: Dumpster
description: Six-yard front-load waste container. Standard kerbside occluder at alley and driveway mouths.

label: Covered car
description: Car under a fitted cover: a vehicle-sized mass that is deliberately not classifiable as a vehicle model. Long-term parked.

label: Hedge run
description: Clipped hedge of parametric length and height along +X. The classic sightline problem on a stop-controlled minor approach.

label: Chain-link fence run
description: Chain-link fence of parametric length and height along +X. Partially transparent: it degrades detection without hiding outright.

label: Mailbox cluster
description: Pedestal-mounted cluster mailbox unit with the doors facing +X. Small sidewalk fixture; a reason for pedestrians to stop at a kerb.

label: Bus shelter
description: Glazed transit shelter with a bench, open on the kerb (+Z) side. Hides waiting pedestrians until they step out.

label: Food cart
description: Sidewalk vending cart with a canopy. Draws a queue of pedestrians onto the kerb and blocks the view down the footway.

label: Shopping cart
description: Small rolling wire shopping cart that can enter a roadway from a kerb or parking area and create a low-mass obstacle conflict.

label: Tyre debris
description: Shredded truck retread lying in the lane. Small dark object that must be classified as drivable-over rather than braked for.

label: Cardboard box
description: Empty cardboard box with open flaps. The canonical false-positive obstacle: large enough to trigger a brake, light enough to ignore.

label: Refuse sacks
description: Cluster of tied rubbish bags at the kerb. Ambiguous low mass that narrows the usable lane on collection day.

label: Downed branch
description: Storm-broken tree limb lying across the lane, with foliage still attached. Irregular, partly drivable, partly not.
